current_evidence: The council's 'The planning process' page links this PDF as its 'local validation requirements' (titled '2026 Local Validation List'), and the document heading and footer say 'Updated 10 March 2026'.

issues.detail: The Coal Mining Risk Assessment is the only requirement placed under Householder, but the source explicitly excludes householder applications from it.
issues.evidence: Item 4: 'ground excavations/foundation works (excluding householder applications and minor works such as fences) ... Development High Risk Referral Areas'

issues.detail: Householder is missing requirements that do apply to it. The Tree Survey applies to building work within 15m of trees, and the source explicitly covers householder excavations within 15m of trees. The Heritage Statement applies to sites in or next to Conservation Areas or within the setting of listed buildings. The Flood Risk Assessment applies to all new development in Flood Zones 2 and 3.
issues.evidence: Item 20 Tree Survey: 'Any planning application for building work or an engineering operation where there are trees located on or within 15m' (householder excavations specifically referenced); Item 13 Heritage Statement; Item 10 FRA

issues.detail: The Affordable Housing Statement is missing as a requirement. It is required for residential developments of 15 units or more and must give details of M4(1)/M4(2)/M4(3) units, with a viability appraisal where the scheme is non-compliant. It appears only indirectly in the S106 Heads of Terms row.
issues.evidence: Item 1 Affordable Housing Statement - Required for: 'Residential developments of 15 units or more'

issues.detail: Several design documents are not captured as separate requirements. These are the Building for a Healthy Life Assessment and the National Design Guide Assessment (both for major residential schemes of 10+ dwellings) and the Whole Life Carbon Assessment (all major developments). BHL appears only by accident, inside the trigger text of a row mislabelled 'Design and Access Statement'. Whole Life Carbon is not mentioned at all.
issues.evidence: Item 3: 'Building for a healthy life (BHL) Assessment Required for: Major Residential schemes (10 or more dwelling units) National Design Guide Assessment Required for: Major residential schemes'; Item 8: 'A Whole Life Carbon Assessment will be required for all major developments'

issues.detail: Nearly every requirement (about 25 rows) carries the note 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', while Outline and Reserved matters are marked '(none)'. The list's triggers are written by development type and scale, not application type. FRA, Transport Assessment, Ecology, Contaminated Land, Coal Mining, Air Quality, Noise and others clearly apply to outline and reserved matters applications too. Saying there are 'no local requirements' for Outline is wrong.
issues.evidence: Item 10 FRA: 'Major development (1 hectare or greater) in Flood Zone 1; all new development in Flood Zones 2 and 3'; Item 19 Transport thresholds apply regardless of application type

issues.detail: The Flood Risk Assessment is placed under 'Change of use - prior approval' only because its guidance mentions 'change of use to a more vulnerable class'. The local list is not a prior approval list. Meanwhile 'Demolition in cons area' is marked '(none)', although the Heritage Statement is required for relevant demolitions in Conservation Areas.
issues.evidence: Item 13 Heritage Statement - Required for: 'Applications for Listed Building Consent' and 'Relevant demolitions that require planning permission in a Conservation Area'

issues.detail: The Listed building consent row is named 'Schedule of works (listed building)', taken from guidance text. The actual requirement is the Heritage Statement (with the schedule of works as part of it). The Heritage Statement row is filed under Full planning only.
issues.evidence: Item 13: Heritage Statement 'Required for: Applications for Listed Building Consent'

issues.detail: Many trigger excerpts are guidance sentences rather than the 'Required for' text, so the thresholds are lost. Arboricultural row: AMS sentence instead of 'trees on or within 15m of the site'. Contaminated Land: 'issues of land contamination are appropriately considered...' instead of 'where contamination is known or suspected'. Drainage/SuDS: 'to use SuDS unless...' instead of 'Major Developments'. Energy/Sustainability: no threshold (10+ dwellings; non-residential 1,000m2+). Heritage: 'necessary in a Heritage Statement will vary...'. Foul sewage and Structural survey are also guidance fragments. Viability starts mid-sentence at '106 agreement...'.
issues.evidence: Item 8: 'Residential schemes of 10+ units' / 'Non-residential schemes of 1,000m2 + floorspace'; Item 11: 'Major Developments'; Item 5: 'Where contamination is known or suspected'

issues.detail: The Environmental Statement (EIA) row's trigger is a sentence from the Coal Mining item ('If an ES is required it is suggested that the CMRA is included within the ES'). The real trigger is Schedule 1 EIA development, or Schedule 2 development where a Screening Opinion requires EIA.
issues.evidence: Item 9 Environmental Statement: Schedule 1 / Schedule 2 development requiring EIA

issues.detail: Several triggers are cut off or incomplete. Transport Assessment/Travel Plan gives only the generic NPPF sentence and omits the local GFA/unit threshold table (e.g. C3 dwellings 80 units, food retail 800m2, B2 4,000m2, B8 5,000m2). Health Impact Assessment lists only 100+ dwellings and omits non-residential 5,000m2+, hot food takeaways and other relevant majors. Statement of Community Involvement omits departures and all major applications. Retail Impact is cut off before the 2,500/1,000/500m2 thresholds. LVIA omits 100+ dwellings, masterplan sites, renewable energy and minerals/waste triggers.
issues.evidence: Item 19 threshold table; Item 12 HIA triggers; Item 17: 'Departures; housing on sites above 0.4ha contrary to the Local Plan; major applications'; Item 18 floorspace thresholds

issues.detail: The 'Submission rules' tab item is a garbled fragment of reference links and policy background, not a requirement. The 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' row is a sentence describing what a Planning Statement should contain, not a separate requirement.
issues.evidence: Tab item text: 'Barnsley Building Heights Study: a%20%20appendix.pdf Barnsley Landscape Character Assessment update... Policy background NPPF...'

issues.detail: The Biodiversity Net Gain row's trigger is a fragment ('...Policy background NPPF BMBC Local Plan Policies BIO1, GI1 ... Barn Conversions SPD 8.') with no trigger. In the source, BNG sits within Item 7 Ecology Survey and a separate Biodiversity Appendix linked from the planning page.
issues.evidence: Planning page links 'biodiversity appendix' alongside the local validation requirements

issues.detail: tab_items holds only 2 entries: a site-layout annotation note, which actually comes from the Masterplan/Design Code Compliance Statement for 10+ dwelling schemes, and a fragment. Yet the reference row claims 30 requirement items, and the source has 21 numbered requirement headings. The tab does not represent the list.
issues.evidence: Table 3 - Local Validation Requirements (In Alphabetical Order), items 1-21

summary: Grokbot's link is the current 2026 Barnsley local list (updated 10 March 2026), though the List date is slightly wrong. The extraction is weak: Coal Mining is wrongly placed under Householder (which it excludes), the Affordable Housing Statement and Whole Life Carbon requirements are missing, most triggers are guidance fragments without thresholds, and everything is dumped under Full planning.

withdrawn_issues.detail: The List date is recorded as 2026-03-01, but the document is dated 10 March 2026. Grokbot's own Date basis even says 'updated 10 March 2026'.
withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: Not an error: the workbook records every list date at month precision (YYYY-MM-01), and its Date_basis already cites "updated 10 March 2026", so 2026-03-01 is the correct month-level date.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. The workbook stores list dates to the month, so the value is right; only the date-basis label could be better. Not a Grokbot error.
